_note: Levels for The Standing Word. You build with gravity off, then let it in. What holds is decided by the same two rules that decide everything else in v2: a written word is one body, and the six non-connecting letters are where it breaks — so which letter you put at the outboard end decides whether it stays up. Checked by verify_levels.mjs before anyone sees them.

how_it_works.write: Click an empty cell that is on the ground or beside something already there, and the selected letter is written into it. It is spent.
how_it_works.bond: Adjacent letters join into one body along the writing line — westward — unless the eastern one is a letter that never joins what follows (ا د ذ ر ز و).
how_it_works.hold: A body stands if any cell of it rests on something. An ALIF stands on nothing at all, and carries whatever is bonded to it: it is a single upright stroke, and holding a frame is what that means.
how_it_works.gravity: Off while you build. Letting it in is the move that ends the level.

levels.name: The Outboard Letter
levels.brief: Two letters, two marks, and gravity waiting. One of them joins nothing after it — so only one order stands.
levels.teaches: A written word is one body, and the six letters that never join what follows are where it breaks. Rāʾ can sit INSIDE a word quite happily — what it cannot do is carry anything hanging off its far side. Put it at the outboard end and it is joined to nothing.

levels.name: The Upright Stroke
levels.brief: Three marks, and the pier reaches only the first. Nothing in your hand joins far enough.
levels.teaches: Alif is a single upright stroke and the only letter that holds a frame — so it is the only one that stands on nothing. It also joins nothing after it, which is why it cannot simply be added to the end of a word: it holds itself, and whatever is bonded to it.
